BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT
Auto MRP with % Wise Procurement Setup
WFX System | Shahi Exports Pvt. Ltd.

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 5 rows · columns: Document Title (text), Business Requirements Document – Auto MRP with % Wise Procurement (text) · identifiers: Document Title]
| Document Title | Business Requirements Document – Auto MRP with % Wise Procurement |
| Module | WFX – Material Requirement Planning (MRP) |
| Prepared For | Shahi Exports Pvt. Ltd. |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft |
| Date | 22 June 2026 |

# 1. Executive Summary
This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the functional requirements for the Auto MRP (Material Requirement Planning) feature to be implemented in WFX for Shahi Exports Pvt. Ltd. The key enhancement involves introducing a percentage-based procurement release mechanism at the article color and size line level, enabling merchandising teams to release material indents.

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 0 rows · columns: Business Problem: Merchandising teams currently have no controlled mechanism to release material indents in partial percentages across multiple MRP runs. This leads to either over-procurement risk or manual workarounds outside the system. The proposed solution introduces a configurable Release % field that governs how much of the open requirement is released at each MRP run cycle. (empty)]
| Business Problem: Merchandising teams currently have no controlled mechanism to release material indents in partial percentages across multiple MRP runs. This leads to either over-procurement risk or manual workarounds outside the system. The proposed solution introduces a configurable Release % field that governs how much of the open requirement is released at each MRP run cycle. |

• Auto MRL (Material Requirement List) generation in WFX at Material article/Color/Size level

## 2.2 Out of Scope
• Production Order quantity — remains 100% of Order Qty; unaffected by Release %

# 4. Functional Requirements

## 4.1 Auto MRP Generation
The system shall automatically generate a Material Requirement List (MRL) in WFX at defined trigger points (e.g., order confirmation, planning milestone). The MRL acts as the source for MRP runs.
• Auto MRP must run at the style/article/Color/Size line level
• MRL generation must consider BOM consumption rates and confirmed order quantities
• Generated MRL must be visible in the MRP Pending List

PD Remarks: As per above written part MRL and MRP part are conflicting each other can you explain how MRL will run as a source of MRP run?
And also we are not clear what you are stating from the statement: “Generated MRL must be visible in the MRP Pending List” kindly clarify.

## 4.2 MRP Pending List Screen
A dedicated MRP Pending List screen must be available in WFX with the following behaviour:
• Display all styles for which MRP has been generated but Indent creation is still pending
• A style is removed from the list once Indent Qty equals Required Qty (i.e., fully released)
• User can search / filter by style, buyer, season, or OC number
• User can select one or multiple Summary OCs for the same style to consolidate into one MRP run

PD Remarks: When system is working on Auto Run MRP, how will system get to know about OC consolidation, and at what stage user will be going to do this consolidation?

## 4.3 MRP Screen – % Wise Procurement Release
This is the core enhancement. At the MRP screen (Level 2), the following new columns and interaction model must be supported:
PD Remarks: Also Let us know what is expected by client in case of fabric process involved in fabric procurement.

### 4.3.1 MRP Screen Column Definitions

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 6 rows · columns: S.No (integer), Field Name (text), Description (text)]
| S.No | Field Name | Description |
| 1 | Required Qty | Current Required Quantity as per BOM Consumption × Order Quantity. Represents the total material needed for the order. |
| 2 | Open to Release Qty | Pending quantity yet to be released from the total Required Qty. Calculated as: Required Qty − Previous Released Qty. |
| 3 | Previous Released Qty | Total quantity already released in prior MRP runs. Reflects cumulative indent quantities already created. |
| 4 | Release % | User-defined procurement percentage input. Determines what portion of Open to Release Qty will be converted to an indent in this run. |
| 5 | Released Qty | Quantity to be released in current run = Open to Release Qty × Release %. This feeds directly into Indent creation. |
| 6 | Indent Qty | Cumulative total indent quantity = Previous Released Qty + Released Qty. |

# 5. Worked Example – Phased Procurement Over 3 MRP Runs
The table below illustrates how a procurement team would release 1,000 units of a material across three MRP runs using the Release % mechanism. The buyer setup defaults to 80%, with a final top-up run at 100%.

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 3 rows · columns: Run (text), Required Qty (integer), Open to Release Qty (integer), Previous Release Qty (integer), Release % (percent), Released Qty (integer), Indent Qty (integer)]
| Run | Required Qty | Open to Release Qty | Previous Release Qty | Release % | Released Qty | Indent Qty |
| First MRP | 1,000 | 1,000 | 0 | 80% | 800 | 800 |
| Second MRP | 1,000 | 200 | 800 | 80% | 160 | 960 |
| Third MRP | 1,000 | 40 | 960 | 100% | 40 | 1,000 |

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 0 rows · columns: Interpretation:
Run 1: 80% of 1,000 = 800 units released. Indent raised for 800 units.
Run 2: Open balance = 200. 80% of 200 = 160 units. Cumulative indent = 960.
Run 3: Open balance = 40. 100% released to fully cover the requirement. Cumulative indent = 1,000. (empty)]
| Interpretation:
Run 1: 80% of 1,000 = 800 units released. Indent raised for 800 units.
Run 2: Open balance = 200. 80% of 200 = 160 units. Cumulative indent = 960.
Run 3: Open balance = 40. 100% released to fully cover the requirement. Cumulative indent = 1,000. |
PD Remarks: In case, system auto – run the MRP based on the configuration which is 80%, and now the Indent qty will be released as per 100 qty. Now user add some new row in the BOM. Now will the system run the MRP for new added article in the BOM or should run the MRP for all item based on “Open to Release Qty”. Kindly Clarify?

# 6. Validations & Business Rules

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 8 rows · columns: # (integer), Validation / Business Rule (text)]
| # | Validation / Business Rule |
| 1 | Release % must be a numeric value only. Non-numeric input must be rejected with a user-friendly error message. |
| 2 | Release % field must be user-editable at the MRP line item level. |
| 3 | System must auto-populate Release % from Buyer-wise Auto MRP Setup configuration, if defined. |
| 4 | User must have the option to define % at header level on MRP Level 2, with a 'Copy Below' or 'Copy to All' option to apply the value to all line items. |
| 5 | Released Qty must not exceed Open to Release Qty. System should validate and prevent over-release. |
| 6 | Production Order generation must always be based on 100% of order quantity, unaffected by Release % logic. |
| 7 | MRP should only appear in the Pending MRP list if Indent creation is still pending (i.e., Indent Qty < Required Qty). |
| 8 | User must be able to consolidate multiple Summary OCs for the same Style in a single MRP run. |

2. Manual Re-Run Capability
• In case of any failure or error during scheduler execution, can the MRP be manually re-run?
• If yes, what will be the reprocessing logic?
3. Scheduler Execution Frequency
• How is the MRP Scheduler expected to run?
• Will it be configured on a day-wise, hour-wise, or custom interval basis?
4. MRP Scheduler Screen Layout
• How should the data be displayed in the MRP Scheduler screen?
• What columns, filters, statuses, and summary information are expected?
5. Created By / Created On Fields
• In the MRP Scheduler screen, do the Created By and Created On fields refer to the Sales Order/OC creation details or the MRP Scheduler execution details?
6. MRP Hierarchy Levels
• What is the expected maximum hierarchy level that the Auto MRP Scheduler should process?
• Should it support Sub-BOMs, Recipes, Yarn, and other lower-level dependencies?
• If Buyer Does not filled any percentage then what would be the approach.
7. Stock Adjustment Logic
• How should stock adjustments impact MRP calculations?
• Should adjusted stock be considered immediately during requirement planning?
8. MRP Replanning on Cancelled and Reactivated Orders
• As per the requirement:
"Cancelled OC would have halted MRP. Reactivation must re-plan all open material requirements from the current already-produced state."
• Kindly clarify:
• How will the system identify the current production status?
• Will MRP consider already produced quantities, issued materials, WIP stock, and procured quantities while replanning?
• Will the reactivated order trigger MRP automatically or through scheduler/manual execution?
9. If no Buyer is mapped with the Released Percentage, then how will system going to work.
10. In case of Confirmed order received no size is there and no previous history so what to do & also about production ?

# 7. Buyer-Wise Auto MRP Setup
A configuration screen must be available (typically under Admin / Setup) to define default Release % values at the Buyer level. This setup drives automatic population of the Release % field when the user runs MRP for styles belonging to that buyer.

[TABLE 8: Table 8 · 4 rows · columns: Configuration Parameter (text), Type (text), Behaviour (text) · identifiers: Configuration Parameter]
| Configuration Parameter | Type | Behaviour |
| Buyer Code / Name | Lookup / Dropdown | Select the buyer for whom the default % is being set |
| Default Release % | Numeric (0–100) | Auto-populated at MRP run time when buyer matches |
| Override Allowed | Yes / No toggle | If Yes, user can edit the pre-filled % at runtime |
| Effective From Date | Date | Date from which the setup takes effect |

# 8. End-to-End User Flow
• System runs Auto MRL for all styles with active orders based on BOM consumption.
• Styles with pending indent creation appear in the MRP Pending List screen.
• Merchandising user opens the Pending List and searches for the desired style.
• User selects one or more Summary OCs for the same style (multi-select for consolidation).
• User clicks 'Run MRP for Indent Generation' to open the MRP Level 2 screen.
• System auto-populates Release % from Buyer-wise setup (if configured).
• User reviews and optionally edits Release % at header level or line level (with Copy to All option).
• System calculates Released Qty = Open to Release Qty × Release %.
• User reviews Released Qty and Indent Qty columns and confirms.
• System creates the Indent for the Released Qty and updates Previous Released Qty for next run.
• Style remains in Pending List until Indent Qty = Required Qty; then it drops off.

PD Remarks: Kindly Clarify 11th line, as it is contradicting with the statement written above in “Validation & Business Rule” line 7.

# 9. Non-Functional Requirements

[TABLE 9: Table 9 · 5 rows · columns: Attribute (text), Requirement (text) · identifiers: Attribute]
| Attribute | Requirement |
| Performance | MRP Pending List must load within 3 seconds for up to 500 pending styles |
| Data Integrity | Previous Released Qty must be locked / read-only; only Release % is user-editable |
| Auditability | All Release % changes and indent generations must be logged with user ID and timestamp |
| Concurrency | Concurrent MRP runs for the same style by different users must be handled with locking |
| Backward Compatibility | Production Order generation must not be impacted by this change under any scenario |

# 10. Glossary

[TABLE 10: Table 10 · 7 rows · columns: Term (text), Definition (text) · identifiers: Term]
| Term | Definition |
| MRP | Material Requirement Planning – process of calculating material needs based on orders and BOM |
| MRL | Material Requirement List – auto-generated list of material requirements for active styles |
| BOM | Bill of Materials – list of raw materials and components required per unit of a style |
| Indent | Purchase Indent – an internal procurement request raised against a material requirement |
| OC | Order Confirmation – confirmed buyer order in WFX |
| Release % | User-defined percentage determining what portion of open requirement is released as indent |
| WFX | The ERP / PLM platform used by Shahi Exports for order and procurement management |
